real_qa.q: How much crude oil is required to manufacture a conventional queen-size polyurethane mattress?
real_qa.r: A conventional queen-size bed with polyurethane foam inside requires 20 gallons of crude oil to make that polyurethane foam. Polyurethane foam is sometimes called solid gasoline because it ignites easily even with cancer-causing flame-retardant chemicals inside.

real_qa.q: What percentage of mattresses are recycled versus landfilled in the United States annually?
real_qa.r: The U.S. throws out 18 million mattresses every single year, and nationally only about 19 percent of them get recycled. The rest are landfilled, incinerated, or in many cases illegally dumped into waters.

real_qa.q: How many different chemicals are used in the manufacturing of a conventional mattress?
real_qa.r: There are over 100 different chemicals that go into making a conventional mattress, which Aaron Schultz argues is as harmful, if not more harmful, than a pesticide-sprayed piece of produce.

real_qa.q: How much landfill space does a single mattress occupy when disposed?
real_qa.r: A single mattress can take up about 32 cubic feet of landfill space. Because those materials are compressed and interwoven, most curbside recycling programs won't even take them.

real_qa.q: What is the carbon footprint of one conventional foam mattress across its full lifecycle?
real_qa.r: One life cycle assessment put a conventional foam mattress at around 368 kilograms of CO2 total, factoring in materials, manufacturing, transport, and disposal, with manufacturing alone accounting for 40 kilograms of that footprint.
real_qa.requete: conventional foam mattress carbon footprint 368 kg CO2

real_qa.q: Which four US states have mandatory mattress recycling programs and what is the consumer recycling fee?
real_qa.r: Only four states—California, Connecticut, Oregon, and Rhode Island—have laws requiring mattress recycling programs run under the Mattress Recycling Council. A small recycling fee gets added at the point of sale, usually between $16 to $22 depending on the state.
